English: Market Stalls
Makeshift wooden stalls and canvas awnings thrown up in a central clearing, drawing in local traders and peasants with simple wares and produce.
Covered Bazaar
A bustling bazaar of timber and cloth, with basic weather protection, encouraging traveling merchants and commerce to thrive year-round.
Stone Market Hall
A sturdy stone building at the heart of the district, providing safe storage, shelter, and permanent booths for traders and artisans.
Weighhouse
A civic building where goods are officially weighed and measured to ensure fair trade and taxation, increasing trust and accountability.
Guild Market
A protected, semi-private complex of shops and warehouses administered by powerful merchant guilds, hosting fairs and specialty trade.
Trade Plaza
A paved open square ringed by merchant houses and shops, hosting regular markets and civic events, and bustling with visitors and commerce.
Merchant Row
A thriving avenue lined with multi-story timber houses, workshops, and specialized shops, attracting wealthy guilds and foreign traders.
Counting House
A fortified building staffed by clerks and scribes, handling contracts, loans, and the citys accounts, securing wealth and enabling greater financial administration.
Exchange Square
A grand open court surrounded by banking houses and merchant palaces, where contracts and letters of credit are exchanged and fortunes are made.
Grand Mercantile Quarter
An entire city district dominated by vast trade halls, permanent fairs, international exchanges, and luxurious guildhouses, the economic heart of the city and region.
